# MuscleOnGLP

> Evidence-based, fully-cited guides to preserving lean muscle mass while losing weight on GLP-1 medications (semaglutide / Ozempic / Wegovy, tirzepatide / Mounjaro / Zepbound). Sold as instant-download PDFs.

- [Full text of every free article and calculator, with citations](https://getmuscleonglp.com/llms-full.txt)

## Products

### The full handbook — $19
"Preserving Lean Mass on GLP-1 Therapy," 33 pages, 54 references. Covers the medications, injection technique, resistance-training routines (gym and bodyweight-only), a protein strategy for a suppressed appetite, running and concurrent training, supplements, micronutrients, side effects, and the post-medication maintenance phase.
- [Buy the handbook](https://getmuscleonglp.com/#pricing)

Each takes one problem and answers it in full. [Index](https://getmuscleonglp.com/guides/)

- [The Protein Playbook](https://getmuscleonglp.com/guides/protein-playbook/): hitting your protein target on a suppressed appetite: the g/kg lookup table, four rules, per-meal distribution, a USDA food table, and three worked sample days.
- [Creatine on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/guides/creatine-glp1/): what the ISSN position stand and the meta-analyses say, the kidney myth, the early water-weight rise on the scale, and the fact that no trial has tested creatine specifically in GLP-1 users.
- [The No-Gym Plan](https://getmuscleonglp.com/guides/no-gym-plan/): a full 12-week bodyweight-only program: progression ladders, two sessions, RPE guidance, pull substitutions without a bar, and a minimum viable session for nausea days.
- [The GLP-1 Off-Ramp](https://getmuscleonglp.com/guides/off-ramp/): coming off the medication: the STEP 1 extension regain data, sarcopenic obesity, why strength rather than lean mass is the outcome to track, and a 12-week off-ramp timeline.

## Free articles (Learn)
- [GLP-1 macros: protein, carbs and fat](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-macros/): set protein first at 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg (2025 joint advisory; benefit levels off near 1.6 g/kg, Morton 2018), fat at 20 to 35% of calories (National Academies AMDR), carbohydrate as the remainder with a 130 g/day RDA floor, fiber at 14 g per 1,000 kcal (Dietary Guidelines). Worked example: 1,725 kcal gives 152 g protein, 48 g fat, 171 g carbohydrate, 24 g fiber.
Full, fully-cited explainers with no paywall. [Index](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/)

- [Does Ozempic cause muscle loss?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/ozempic-muscle-loss/): roughly 15-40% of GLP-1 weight loss is lean mass; the SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy measured about 26% for tirzepatide; resistance training and protein are the countermeasures.
- [How much protein do you need on a GLP-1?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/protein-on-glp1/): about 1.6-2.2 g/kg for lean-mass retention (a four-society advisory recommends 1.2-1.6 g/kg during active loss); only ~43% of users hit a modest minimum.
- [Creatine and GLP-1s: is it safe with Ozempic or Zepbound?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/creatine-and-ozempic/): the ISSN safety data, the serum-creatinine measurement artifact (not kidney damage), and the honest limit that no trial has tested creatine specifically in GLP-1 users.
- [Can you keep muscle without a gym?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/build-muscle-glp1-no-gym/): a 2023 meta-analysis found no meaningful difference between free weights and machines; the same principle supports progressed bodyweight training.
- [What happens to your muscle when you stop Ozempic?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/muscle-after-stopping-ozempic/): the STEP 1 extension regain data (about two-thirds within a year), sarcopenic obesity, and why strength is the outcome to track.
- [Ozempic vs Mounjaro vs Zepbound: which preserves more muscle?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/ozempic-vs-mounjaro-vs-zepbound-muscle/): the trials were separate and used different methods, so cross-trial lean-mass comparisons are limited; a larger total loss puts more absolute muscle at stake.
- [Signs you are losing muscle, not just fat](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/signs-of-muscle-loss-glp1/): why the scale and even DXA lean-mass numbers mislead, and why tracked strength is the best signal you can check at home.
- [The best exercises to preserve muscle](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/best-exercises-preserve-muscle-glp1/): resistance training offset about 93.5% of diet-induced lean-mass loss in a meta-analysis; train the major compound movement patterns and progress them.
- [GLP-1 muscle loss by the numbers](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-muscle-loss-statistics/): the lean-mass share, protein shortfall, persistence and regain figures in one place.
- [Can you build new muscle on a GLP-1?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/build-new-muscle-on-glp1/): preserving versus gaining muscle during weight loss, and what training and protein make possible.
- [Whey, plant, or collagen: the best protein on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/best-protein-for-muscle-on-glp1/): protein quality and leucine content for muscle retention when appetite is small.
- [Best protein shakes for GLP-1 users: a 5-point label checklist](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/best-protein-shakes-glp1/): 25-30 g protein (about 2.5-3 g leucine) per serving, a complete source, a nausea-friendly format, and third-party testing.
- [How to fuel workouts on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/fuel-workouts-glp1/): total daily protein beats timing (Schoenfeld 2013 meta-analysis), about 25-30 g protein after training, fluids, and the hypoglycemia caution with insulin or sulfonylureas.
- [High-protein GLP-1 meal plan: a sample day with grams](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-high-protein-meal-plan/): five small servings totalling about 107 g of protein (USDA values), scaled by 1.2-1.6 g/kg, with nausea-day swaps.
- [Protein timing on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-protein-timing-muscle/): per-meal distribution (about 25-30 g per meal) for people eating less.
- [Retatrutide and muscle loss](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/retatrutide-muscle-loss/): the published Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 weight results (NEJM, September 2026) and what body-composition data exists for the investigational triple agonist.
- [GLP-1s and muscle loss in women over 50](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-muscle-loss-women-over-50/): menopause, sarcopenia risk and bone.
- [GLP-1s, bone density and fracture risk](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-bone-density-fracture-risk/): the DXA and fracture evidence.
- [Cardio vs. weights on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/cardio-vs-weights-glp1/): why resistance training, not cardio alone, protects lean mass.
- [Resting heart rate on a GLP-1](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-resting-heart-rate/): how much Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound raise resting heart rate (label and meta-analysis figures), why it often eases after dose escalation, the habits that lower it, and when to call a prescriber.
- [Is a DEXA or InBody scan worth it on a GLP-1?](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/dexa-inbody-scan-glp1/): what body-composition scans can and cannot tell you.
- [High-protein meals and shakes for nausea days](https://getmuscleonglp.com/learn/glp1-high-protein-meals-nausea/): protein that stays down on a GLP-1.
## Free calculators
Each runs in the browser, cites its sources on the page, and gives no dosing advice. [Index](https://getmuscleonglp.com/tools/)

- [GLP-1 weight loss calculator](https://getmuscleonglp.com/weight-loss-calculator/): applies the average weight loss from each drug's main trial to your weight: Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg) 14.9% over 68 weeks in STEP 1; Zepbound/Mounjaro (tirzepatide) 15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9% at 5, 10 and 15 mg over 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1; semaglutide 1 mg and 2.4 mg with type 2 diabetes 7.0% and 9.6% in STEP 2. Also estimates the lean-mass share of the loss.
- [GLP-1 muscle loss calculator](https://getmuscleonglp.com/muscle-loss-calculator/): the share of GLP-1 weight loss likely to be lean mass, with versus without enough protein and resistance training.
- [GLP-1 calorie, protein and macro calculator](https://getmuscleonglp.com/protein-calculator/): calorie target (Mifflin-St Jeor), daily protein target (1.6 to 2.2 g/kg, with the 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg GLP-1 advisory range), grams per meal, and macros at the target: fat at 25% of calories, carbohydrate as the remainder, fiber at 14 g per 1,000 kcal.
- [Protein food calculator](https://getmuscleonglp.com/protein-food-calculator/): adds up servings of 13 common foods (USDA FoodData Central values, e.g. chicken breast 31 g per 100 g, low-fat cottage cheese 28 g per cup, a large egg 6 g) against a 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg daily protein target, the range of the 2025 four-society joint advisory on nutrition during GLP-1 therapy.
- [Weight-regain (off-ramp) calculator](https://getmuscleonglp.com/off-ramp-calculator/): projected regain after stopping, from the STEP 1 extension.
## Key evidence-based facts (each cited in the guides)
- Average weight loss in the main trials: 14.9% on semaglutide 2.4 mg at 68 weeks (STEP 1, placebo 2.4%); 15.0-20.9% on tirzepatide 5-15 mg at 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1, placebo 3.1%); 9.6% on semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes (STEP 2). Individual results vary widely around these averages.
- A substantial fraction of GLP-1 weight loss is lean mass: reviews place it at roughly 15-40% of total weight lost; the SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy measured about 26% for tirzepatide (74% fat, 26% lean).
- Protein target for lean-mass retention during weight loss: approximately 1.6-2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (vs the 0.8 g/kg RDA). A GLP-1-specific advisory from four medical societies recommends 1.2-1.6 g/kg during active weight reduction.
- Only about 43% of GLP-1 users met even a modest protein minimum in a cross-sectional study; GLP-1 medications reduce energy intake by roughly a quarter in controlled studies.
- Resistance training during caloric restriction offset ~93.5% of diet-induced lean-mass loss (+0.82 kg preserved) in a meta-analysis of older adults.
- Muscle growth does not differ meaningfully between free weights, machines, and bodyweight training when appropriately loaded and progressed (2023 meta-analysis, 13 studies, 1,016 participants).
- Creatine added ~1.37 kg more lean tissue mass than resistance training alone in a meta-analysis of older adults. The ISSN position stand reports no compelling evidence of harm in otherwise healthy people at intakes studied up to 30 g/day for 5 years. Creatine raises serum creatinine as a measurement artifact, not as kidney damage.
- About two-thirds of lost weight was regained within a year of stopping semaglutide (STEP 1 trial extension: 17.3% net loss at end of treatment, 5.6% one year later); ~65% of 125,474 real-world users discontinued within 12 months.

## Explicit limits of the evidence (stated in the guides, not glossed over)
- The STEP trials did not measure fat-versus-muscle composition during the weight-regain phase. Claims that regained weight is "all fat" are not supported by those trials.
- No published trial has tested creatine supplementation specifically in people taking GLP-1 medications. The creatine evidence is extrapolated from resistance-training and older-adult populations.
- Lean-tissue loss is an unreliable predictor of strength change: short-to-mid-term GLP-1 trials showed statistically preserved handgrip strength despite lean-mass reductions, while longer-term research in older adults with type 2 diabetes has reported reductions in handgrip strength.

## Important
This is educational content, not medical advice. It gives no medical or dosing advice and does not cover obtaining or sourcing medication. The split-dose calculator only does arithmetic on the prescription numbers a reader enters; readers are directed to confirm any change with their prescriber or pharmacist. Not affiliated with Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, or any medication manufacturer.
Some content, including summaries, illustrations and share images, is generated or assembled with automated and AI tools and checked before publishing; data charts are drawn from the cited figures. See the [editorial policy](https://getmuscleonglp.com/editorial-policy/) and [Terms of Service](https://getmuscleonglp.com/terms/) section 3.
